candidates.title: Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes
candidates.authors: Alex Buckley, Carlo Vetralla, Brendan Rose, Jash Gada, Gabrielle Servito, Antonina Hafner, Sedona Murphy, Michael Mui, Alistair Nicol Boettiger, Daniele Canzio
candidates.abstract: Abstract Heterochromatin typically represses genes 1,2 , yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation 3–7 . How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent 8 . In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self–non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly 8 . By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer–promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

candidates.title: Unconventional resistivity reduction in NbP semimetal nanoribbons
candidates.authors: Haotian Su, Sauviz Alaei, Áshildur Friðriksdóttir, Sydney Fultz-Waters, Hyeonhu Bae, Xiangjin Wu, Yufei Zhao, Donglai Zhong, Tara Peña, Matthew J. Hurley, Yujun Deng, Sandesh Kalantre, Andrew J. Barnum, Gregory Pitner, Sam Vaziri, Xinyu Bao, Zhi-Xun Shen, David Goldhaber-Gordon, Paul C. McIntyre, Shan X. Wang, Aaron Sharpe, Yuri Suzuki, Binghai Yan, Eric Pop
candidates.abstract: Modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering. To circumvent this unwanted behaviour, here, we explore the fundamental limits of charge transport in topological semimetal niobium phosphide (NbP) nanoribbons down to approximately 6-nm widths, with industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication. The extracted NbP nanoribbon resistivity reaches 18 ± 4.1 μΩ cm at room temperature with an approximately 9-nm2 cross-sectional area, lower than that of conventional metals and semimetals with comparable size. The NbP nanoribbon resistivity decreases with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper. This trend suggests a growing relative contribution of surface and edge states as the nanoribbon cross-section is reduced, despite a certain amount of disorder, including edge roughness. Our findings advance the understanding of size-dependent transport and scaling in this class of semimetals, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects in future nanoelectronics. Niobium phosphide semimetal nanoribbons show decreasing resistivity with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects via industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication.

candidates.title: Context-dependent response of endothelial cells to PIK3CA mutation
candidates.authors: Helena Sabata, Ariadna Roca-Coll, Jose A. Dengra, Ane Martinez-Larrinaga, Jorge Andrade, Elena Castillo-Agea, Leonor Gouveia, Maria Garrido-Cruz, Alberto Collado-Remacha, Frederico Água, Sandra D. Castillo, Nathalie Tisch, Macarena De Andrés-Laguillo, Sophie Payne, Judith Llena, Svanhild Nornes, Pilar Villacampa, Dorota Szumska, Ana Rita Grosso, Karina Yaniv, Bart Vanhaesebroeck, María P. Alcolea, Sarah De Val, Susana Lopez-Fernandez, Katrien De Bock, Eulalia Baselga, Rui Benedito, Michael Potente, Ana Angulo-Urarte, Mariona Graupera
candidates.abstract: Cancer-associated mutations in PIK3CA underlie congenital overgrowth disorders that frequently involve the vasculature1,2. Among the affected tissues, the endothelium commonly exhibits aberrant expansion, leading to vascular malformations3. Notably, these lesions arise predominantly in veins and capillaries, whereas arteries are largely spared, for reasons that remain unclear. Here, using genetic lineage tracing, we show that endothelial expression of PIK3CAH1047R drives profound clonal expansion of capillary and venous endothelial cells, whereas mature arterial endothelial cells are refractory to pathological PI3K activation. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features, providing a mechanistic explanation for the paucity of arterial lesions after PIK3CA genetic perturbation. Mechanistically, these effects are mediated by two complementary downstream branches of PI3K signalling: increased proliferation, which drives vascular overgrowth, and upregulation of the venous-specifying transcription factor NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), which suppresses arterial differentiation. Together, our findings reveal that pathogenic responses to PIK3CAH1047R are dictated by endothelial differentiation state and fate trajectory, and demonstrate that arterial endothelium is intrinsically resistant to oncogenic PI3K signalling. Arteries are therefore shielded from PIK3CA mutations, explaining the rarity of arterial malformations in PIK3CA-driven disease. candidates.title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage
candidates.authors: Jevan B. Yu, Etienne Fluet-Chouinard, Susan E. Page, Chris D. Evans, Charles F. Harvey, César Terrer
candidates.abstract: Over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems—a centuries-old practice2,3—causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800–2020 by combining a new flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48–99) mW m−2—equivalent to 2.7 (1.8–3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing—originating from 0.4–0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52–110) mW m−2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (−9 (−15–−2) mW m−2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining currently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate. Reconstruction of radiative forcing resulting from worldwide peatland drainage over the past two centuries reveals a persistent net warming effect caused by the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions over that of avoided CH4 emissions.

candidates.abstract: Slowing climate change requires overcoming inertia in political, technological and geophysical systems1–3. candidates.title: Disturbances and climate drive tree elevational shifts
candidates.authors: Jianmin Wang, Jonathan A. Knott, Grant M. Domke, Brady S. Hardiman, Brian F. Walters, Songlin Fei
candidates.abstract: Abstract Climate change and disturbances are reshaping forest ecosystems worldwide 1–4 , yet their combined effects on species redistribution remain poorly understood. Here we analyse repeated measurements from 44,368 forest inventory plots spanning 1999–2025, with an average remeasurement interval of 10 years, to examine how climate and natural disturbances jointly influence the elevational redistribution of tree species across the western USA. We show that climate warming increased sapling abundance, whereas increasing drought frequency and recent natural disturbances (fire, insect outbreaks and disease) reduced tree abundance, particularly among adult trees. By contrast, legacy fire was associated with increased sapling abundance, with stronger positive responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms. These influences were distributed unevenly across species’ elevational ranges: upper portions of species’ ranges generally experienced stronger warming, greater increases in drought frequency and more disturbance activity than lower portions, creating elevational asymmetries in stress and recovery. These elevational asymmetries were associated with more pronounced downslope shifts in basal area centres, probably reflecting disturbance effects on larger trees. By contrast, stem abundance centres showed more divergent shifts, consistent with sapling responses to both climate change and disturbance. Our findings reveal contrasting demographic responses to climate change and natural disturbances that shape the elevational redistribution of different species, with potential consequences for forest composition, resilience and long-term stability.

candidates.abstract: Highly heritable, polygenic and easily measured, adult height has long been the model trait in human genetics1,2. Although the landscape of height-associated common genetic variation has been studied extensively2, rare variation remains relatively unexplored1. Here, using rare protein-altering variants in a discovery set of 826,066 exomes, we identify 207 height-associated genes, 98% of which replicate in an additional 624,567 individuals. The rarest and most deleterious class of variation, singleton (frequency < 0.0001%) putative loss-of-function variants, implicated 17 genes with large effects on height ranging from −17cm (ACAN) to +11 cm (FBN1) per allele, 52× larger than the average effect of common height-associated variants and comparable to the 1% tails of a common variant polygenic score. Several genes (TET1, DTL and IGF2BP2) have effect sizes that are at least as large as established Mendelian height genes, yet lack documented stature or skeletal growth syndromes, particularly for genes associated with increased height. Our large-scale sequencing study elucidates the genetic architecture and allelic heterogeneity of rare variants in height, providing unique insights into their large effects—often similar to or larger than recognized Mendelian syndromes—and their impact on trait prediction, clinical evaluation, and discovery power to facilitate drug target prioritization. Analysis of exomes from over 1.4 million participants implicates 207 genes, including large effect coding variants and gene burden tests, and demonstrates the utility of large-scale sequencing for trait prediction and variant interpretation.

candidates.abstract: Vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1–7. Whether these cues alone can reconstitute human trunk-like morphogenesis in vitro remains unknown. Here we present a synthetic embryology platform for high-throughput, spatiotemporal delivery of morphogen signals to epithelial cysts derived from human pluripotent stem cells. Transient WNT and BMP gradients are sufficient to drive the generation of axially elongating trunk-like structures that contain a central neural tube flanked by axial, paraxial, intermediate and lateral mesoderm. The geometry of the transient BMP signal exerts lasting control over mediolateral patterning and bilateral symmetry. Patterning and morphogenesis are sustained by neuromesodermal and lateral plate mesoderm progenitors induced by the initial cues, which act as endogenous signalling centres. Together, these findings define a minimal spatial code sufficient to reconstitute trunk-like morphogenesis in a human stem-cell-based model and establish a scalable platform for studying early human development and congenital disorders. A high-throughput synthetic embryology platform reveals how transient spatial cues establish two self-sustaining signalling centres that organize trunk-like morphogenesis, enabling the study of early human development and congenital disorders.

candidates.title: A gut–brain sensory-motor circuit regulates sugar ingestion in Drosophila
candidates.authors: Xinyue Cui, Matthew R. Meiselman, Staci N. Thornton, Sophia Gustin, Jennifer Jeter, Geoffrey W. Meissner, Nilay Yapici
candidates.abstract: Bidirectional communication between the brain and digestive tract is critical for optimizing nutrient preference and food intake, yet the neural mechanisms that couple gut nutrient sensing with ingestive motor control remain poorly understood. Here we identify a gut–brain sensory-motor circuit that regulates sugar ingestion in flies. We show that the brain neurons that regulate food ingestion, IN1s1, receive excitatory input from enteric sensory neurons that penetrate the foregut epithelium and detect sugars in the gut lumen during ingestion. Functional imaging and connectome analyses reveal that IN1s integrate excitatory input from multiple sugar-sensing neurons, including enteric sensory neurons, and provide inhibitory output to enteric motor neurons that control the muscles at the entry of the crop—a stomach-like organ. During ingestion, IN1 activation suppresses these enteric motor neurons, relaxes the crop duct and promotes rapid transfer of food into the crop, thereby enabling sustained food intake. candidates.authors: Giada Finocchio, Seraina Oberli, George D. Lampe, Michael Schmitz, Samuel H. Sternberg, Martin Jinek
candidates.abstract: Abstract CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) achieve site-specific DNA integration by combining the RNA-guided targeting action of a nuclease-deficient CRISPR–Cas system with the assembly of a Tn7-like transpososome complex 1,2 . Understanding the detailed mechanisms of this elaborate process is paramount to engineering CAST systems into programmable genetic tools 3–6 . Type I-F Pseudoalteromonas CAST ( Pse CAST) shows the highest activity in mammalian cells so far 7 and has been adapted extensively through directed evolution 8 . However, its continued rational engineering requires addressing critical gaps in our understanding of transpososome assembly and activation 9 . Here we perform structural analyses using cryogenic electron microscopy, validated by DNA transposition assays, to visualize the Pse CAST system in a series of functional states that define the stepwise mechanism of RNA-guided DNA integration. The structures of the Pse CAST targeting and transposase recruitment complexes revealed that conformational changes in the Cascade–TniQ module, induced by R-loop formation, are associated with target-DNA stabilization and TnsC heptamerization. This, in turn, results in the recruitment of the TnsAB transposase by conserved interactions with the carboxy-terminal tail of TnsB. Finally, the structure of the 1.2 MDa Pse CAST transpososome holocomplex revealed allosteric coupling of TnsC–TnsB and TnsB–target-DNA interactions to the conformational remodelling of the TnsB catalytic site, activating donor-DNA integration. Together, these findings establish a unified mechanistic blueprint for RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CASTs and provide a structural framework to guide their engineering for genome-editing applications.

candidates.authors: Whi Dong Kim, Clément Livache, Ho Jin, Valerio Pinchetti, Tung H. Dang, Oleg V. Kozlov, Heeyoung Jung, Zachary L. Robinson, Victor I. Klimov
candidates.abstract: Colloidal quantum dot solids are promising for photoconversion and photochemistry, but their performance is fundamentally limited by rapid hot-carrier cooling, low carrier mobility and short transport ranges1. Here we demonstrate a spin-exchange-driven phototransport regime in manganese-doped quantum dot films that enables the generation, long-range transport and regeneration of hot carriers. Ultrafast spin-exchange-mediated Auger upconversion promotes electrons into high-energy, delocalized states before phonon cooling2,3, establishing a transient high-mobility conduction channel. Crucially, spin-exchange interactions not only generate hot carriers but also enable their repeated re-excitation, thereby sustaining long-range drift. This mechanism yields room-temperature mobilities of about 150 cm2 V−1 s−1 and submillimetre drift lengths—far greater than those of conventional quantum dot solids and approaching values characteristic of crystalline semiconductors. Time-of-flight measurements confirm drift-dominated transport, with transit times scaling linearly with distance and inversely with electric field. These results establish a route to long-range energy transport in nanoscale materials and enable the use of hot carriers in photoconversion, photochemistry and transit-time-limited photodetection. A phototransport regime driven by spin exchange is demonstrated in manganese-doped quantum dot solids, enabling the generation, long-range transport and regeneration of hot carriers and yielding submillimetre drift lengths.

candidates.authors: Francesco Zatelli, Bart Roovers, Nick van Loo, Antonio Lombardi, Juan D. Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, Vincent P. M. Sietses, Florian J. Bennebroek Evertsz’, Pablo Cova Fariña, Alberto Bordin, Ghada Badawy, Erik P. A. M. Bakkers, Michael Wimmer, Leo P. Kouwenhoven
candidates.abstract: Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their noise sensitivity is expected to decrease exponentially with separation between Majorana zero modes, a suppression known as topological protection1. Kitaev chains in quantum-dot–superconductor arrays can host Majorana zero modes at their ends1,2, even in two-site chains3. These minimal-chain modes, known as poor man’s Majoranas, retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron–hole character, but lack topological protection3–5. A key challenge is moving from identifying these modes in electrical transport to coherent qubit control. Here we demonstrate coherent time-resolved rotations between parity states encoded by four poor man’s Majoranas in two coupled minimal Kitaev chains3,6–8. Total fermion parity conservation separates the system into global even- and odd-parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both, with frequencies matching within 5% at the poor man’s Majorana sweet spot, consistent with largely isolated Majoranas6. The oscillation frequency, rotation axis and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in agreement with our model for short chains. Our results establish coherent control of a qubit encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes, realized using minimal Kitaev chains. They lay the groundwork for universal qubit operations, comprehensive coherence characterization and probing protection in longer chains. Coherent time-resolved rotations between parity states encoded by four poor man’s Majoranas are demonstrated in two coupled minimal Kitaev chains, providing a foundation for topologically protected qubits in longer chains.

candidates.authors: Shaomin Yang, Chunxiang Lan, Miaomiao Zeng, Liqing Wu, Tian Zhang, Mimi Fu, Boyu Yang, Ziwei Zheng, Yu Wu, Jing Guo, Rui Guo, Mi Xu, Rongyan Wen, Zaiwei Wang, Shuangyan Hu, Mostafa Boshta, Jun Chen, Yaoguang Rong, Xiong Li
candidates.abstract: All-perovskite tandem solar cells (TSCs) are gaining prominence due to their ability to surpass the efficiency limit of single-junction perovskite solar cells (PSCs)1,2. However, the efficiency and stability of all-perovskite TSCs are limited by chemical instability at the hole transport layer/perovskite interface in the tin-lead (Sn-Pb) narrow-bandgap subcell, which introduces deep trap states from tin cations and promotes non-radiative recombination3-5. The resulting narrow-bandgap Sn-Pb PSC achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.4% (certified 25.2%) with an open-circuit voltage of 0.92 V and a fill factor of 83.4%. Integrated into monolithic all-perovskite TSCs, the device delivers a PCE of 31.1% (certified 30.8%) together with enhanced thermal (ISOS-D-2I, 85 °C) and operational stability (ISOS-L-1I) under inert conditions.

Dental morphology and proteomic analyses of fossils from southern China identify lineages with and without Denisovan affinity, indicating the diversity of hominin populations in this region in the Middle to Late Pleistocene.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Intratumoural heterogeneity, originating from genetic, epigenetic and phenotypic diversity, is pervasive in cancer and a fundamental barrier to curative treatment 1,2 . How these heterogeneous cell states emerge and co-evolve within tumours remains poorly understood. Here we develop a deep-learning framework that quantifies colorectal cancer tissue architecture and nuclear morphology at subcellular resolution to predict patient outcome. Integrating this with spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence and patient-derived organoids, we identify a co-evolutionary relationship between tumour architecture and cancer cell states. We identify architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer that drive cell state diversification by promoting distinct cancer stem cell programmes. Specifically, tissue fragmentation generates compressive forces that activate YAP, suppressing classical stem cell programmes and inducing fetal/regenerative stem cell states that initially manifest as hybrid states with features of partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Subsequent tumour–stroma communication through TGFβ diversifies these into distinct stem cell and EMT states. Reciprocally, β-catenin activity tunes tumour cell responsiveness to architectural cues. candidates.title: Supersolid crystals of dipolar excitons in a lattice
candidates.authors: C. Morin, C. Lagoin, T. Gupta, N. Reinić, A. Gupta, K. Baldwin, L. Pfeiffer, G. Pupillo, F. Dubin
candidates.abstract: In condensed-matter physics, long-range correlations introduce quantum states of matter that challenge intuition. For example, supersolids combine density order that manifests as symmetry-breaking spatial arrangement, and frictionless superfluid flow. However, supersolids have proven to exist only under very stringent conditions, with evidence limited to a few spontaneously fragmented superfluids observed in the weakly interacting regime. Here we demonstrate a framework to realize crystalline supersolids in the strong-interaction regime, by confining dipolar bosons in a lattice with long-range hopping. We show that dipolar excitons realize this lattice model. At fractional lattice fillings of one-quarter, one-third and one-half, we observe mesoscopic quantum crystals across around 100 sites that spontaneously break the lattice translational symmetry. At the same time, coherent long-range hopping induces off-diagonal long-range order such that the exciton solids are superfluids. Our numerical methods quantitatively confirm that supersolidity builds up in the ground state of the lattice Hamiltonian. Supersolids have previously been observed in weakly interacting scenarios. Now several supersolid phases are demonstrated in a strongly correlated system of dipolar excitons confined to a lattice with long-range hopping.

candidates.abstract: Electrons trapped on solid neon surfaces can serve as low-noise charge qubits with full electrical control and a compact device footprint. Using electrons that are naturally confined in close proximity on the neon surface, we demonstrate strong qubit–qubit coupling and implement the cross-resonance and bSWAP types of two-qubit operations using global microwave drives. Our results indicate that engineering electron confinement on solid neon may enhance control over the qubit–qubit interactions and yield a compact and scalable quantum computing architecture. Now two-qubit gates have been demonstrated using the strong coupling between electrons confined in close proximity to each other.

candidates.abstract: Physical exercise promotes bone health. However, its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. Here, we identified the hepatokine AGP2 as an osteoanabolic mediator of exercise. Exercise increases circulating AGP2 levels in mice and humans. Here, the authors show that in mice exercise stimulates the liver to release AGP2, a hormone-like protein that promotes bone formation and protects against bone loss, revealing a potential treatment strategy for osteoporosis.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Osteoclasts are essential for bone remodeling and homeostasis. Their excessive activation drives pathological bone loss disorders such as periodontitis and arthritis. Current osteoclast-inhibiting therapies are limited by adverse effects and poor specificity, underscoring the importance to identify new regulators of osteoclastogenesis. Here, we conducted a pooled CRISPR–Cas9 screen targeting cluster of differentiation (CD) genes to uncover novel modulators of osteoclast differentiation and identified CD300LD, a single-pass transmembrane protein, as a potent driver of osteoclastogenesis. Cd300ld deletion impaired osteoclastogenesis in cell line and primary bone-marrow–derived macrophages. In vivo, myeloid-specific Cd300ld knockout mice exhibited significantly reduced alveolar bone loss and osteoclast numbers in experimental periodontitis, as well as attenuated joint inflammation and bone erosion in arthritis models, whereas bone remodeling during skeletal development remained unaltered. Mechanistically, cholesterol acts as extracellular activator for CD300LD to activate osteoclastogenesis. Cd300ld deficiency intracellularly inhibited phosphorylation of FES, SYK, and STAT3. Consistently, loss of Fes , Syk or Stat3 recapitulated the Cd300ld -deficient phenotypes, establishing a CD300LD–FES–SYK–STAT3 signaling axis essential for osteoclast differentiation. Together, these findings identify CD300LD as a critical, previously unrecognized driver of osteoclastogenesis and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for inflammatory bone loss.

candidates.authors: Hui Zhang, Jiao Liu, Jikang Cheng, Xingnan Wang, Xinran Yu, Chengshuai He, Shuo Zhang, Hao Wu, Yongsong Cao, Congfen Gao, Yunhao Gao
candidates.abstract: Nanopesticides offer new opportunities to improve pesticide efficacy and utilization efficiency; however, they are often complex to produce and exhibit low cargo loading, except for those formed through molecular self-assembly. Currently, the formation of these self-assembly nanopesticides remains difficult to predict, heavily relying on serendipitous observation and trial-and-error screening. Here, we report that the widely used and environmentally benign biopesticide synergist fluorescent brightener FB-113 drives the self-assembly of various pesticides into nanoparticles with ultrahigh loadings exceeding 80%. We developed an interpretable Quantitative Pesticide Structure-Assembly Prediction model (QPSAP), which reveals hydrophobicity, halogenation, polarity, and topological structure of pesticide molecules as key descriptors associated with FB-113-mediated self-assembly propensity. QPSAP was applied to large-scale virtual screening of a pesticide library to identify novel candidates for FB-113-mediated self-assembly, demonstrating complete concordance between predictions and experimental outcomes in a prospectively tested validation subset. The resulting nanopesticides enhance foliar wetting, adhesion, photostability, and transcuticular penetration, thereby increasing insecticidal and acaricidal efficacy against multiple pests while exhibiting improved crop compatibility and a reduced acute toxicity profile under the tested conditions. This work advances self-assembly nanopesticides from empirical formulation toward predictive, computationally screenable design, representing a significant advancement in safe and efficient pesticide nanoformulations. candidates.abstract: Abstract Self-esteem is a cornerstone of mental health across the lifespan. Throughout life, but particularly during adolescence, self-esteem is shaped by social appraisals. Previous work in adults has shown that momentary fluctuations in self-esteem are explained not only by whether we are liked by others but also by whether we are liked more or less than expected (social prediction errors). Here, we examine age-related differences in how social experiences shape self-esteem in 141 participants aged 10-40 years using an experimental social evaluation task and ecological momentary assessment. In the experiment, self-esteem reactivity to unexpected social feedback follows a non-linear age-related pattern, peaking in late adolescence. In daily life, self-esteem reactivity to perceived pleasantness of social interaction and naturalistic social prediction errors is stronger in younger participants. Individual differences in experimental and daily-life self-esteem reactivity are associated, highlighting heightened self-esteem malleability during adolescence.

candidates.title: Observationally-constrained CMIP6 projections of a snow-free Northern Hemisphere
candidates.authors: Yi Shen, Ting Wei, Bing Chen
candidates.abstract: Northern Hemisphere snow cover retreat poses substantial climate risks, but large uncertainties in Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) hinder accurate projections of future evolution. We develop a monthly emergent constraint based on historical warming trends, which strongly correlate with ablation-season (May–October) snow cover loss. This constraint reduces inter-model variance by 17.0–58.4% under different emission scenarios and rectifies raw CMIP6 snow-loss biases. Constrained projections reveal that under the higher-emission scenario (SSP5-8.5), winter snow cover retreats in arid regions from the 2030 s, and Arctic summers become snow-free by the 2040 s. By mid-century, mid-latitude spring and autumn snow cover disappears, with arid and semi-arid regions approaching year-round snow-free conditions and humid regions losing 1–4 months of seasonal snow cover. Under the most sustainable scenario (SSP1-2.6) snow disappearance is delayed by 7.1–34 years relative to SSP5-8.5 across vulnerable regions and months. Overall, our constraint narrows projection uncertainty by 0.95–11.91 years, delaying projected disappearance by 0.01–2.65 years in transitional months while advancing it by 0.51–4.15 years in midsummer, providing refined month-specific baselines for climate risk assessments. This study presents a monthly emergent constraint based on observed warming that reduces CMIP6 inter-model variance and refines snow-free projections: Arctic summers become snow-free by 2040 s under SSP5-8.5, while snow disappearance is delayed by 7–34 years under SSP1-2.6 in vulnerable regions and months.

candidates.authors: Ryuta Uraki, Kiyoko Iwatsuki-Horimoto, Maki Kiso, Mutsumi Ito, Seiya Yamayoshi, Masaki Imai, Yoshihiro Kawaoka
candidates.abstract: Since early 2024, highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 virus (clade 2.3.4.4b) has caused outbreaks in U.S. dairy cattle, infecting other mammals including humans. Here, we evaluate the protective efficacy of two commercially available seasonal influenza vaccines against a human-derived bovine H5N1 isolate, A/Texas/37/2024, in influenza-naïve female ferrets. All unvaccinated ferrets develop severe disease and succumb to infection or meet humane euthanasia criteria. Immunisation with an inactivated influenza vaccine reduces viral titres in multiple respiratory and extrapulmonary tissues and delays disease progression but does not prevent fatal outcomes. By contrast, five of six ferrets immunised with a live attenuated influenza vaccine survive challenge and show more effective control of viral replication in the nasal mucosa. Live attenuated vaccination induces stronger T-cell responses, while the absence of detectable neutralising activity against the challenge virus suggests that cellular immunity, rather than neutralising antibodies, may contribute to protection. These findings demonstrate that seasonal live attenuated influenza vaccination can provide cross-protection against lethal infection with an antigenically distinct bovine-derived H5N1 virus, potentially through cellular immune responses in the respiratory tract. candidates.authors: Zhaoyang Chen, Alae Eddine Lakraychi, Santosh Thapa, Lihong Zhao, Liqun Guo, Jie Zheng, Yanliang Liang, Dan-Thien Nguyen, Yang-Tse Cheng, Yan Yao
candidates.abstract: All-solid-state batteries offer enhanced safety and high energy density. However, their practical application is challenged by the need for high external pressures, often tens of MPa, to maintain intimate solid–solid contact and preserve ion/electron percolation pathways during cycling. In this work, we demonstrate that low-modulus, low-hardness, creep-compliant, low-strain organic active materials that readily deform in response to external pressures and microstructural changes enable stable cell operation under low stack pressures. Using bis-tetraaminobenzoquinone (TAQ) as a model compound, we show its low modulus (8.4–15.3 GPa), low hardness (0.33–0.76 GPa), and moderate creep compliance (m = 0.038–0.073), quantified by nanoindentation of both pristine and lithiated TAQ, enable adaptive deformability under low stack pressures. TAQ-based solid-state cells achieve stable cycling and promising rate performance at external pressures as low as 1 MPa, retaining 80.3% capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5C. Operando and post-mortem electron microscopy reveal that TAQ electrodes maintain high structural integrity at pressures as low as 0.2 MPa. These findings establish a materials design strategy centered on mechanically adaptive materials to enable solid-state battery operation under practically relevant pressure conditions. Low stack pressure is key for enabling practical solid-state batteries. Here, the authors demonstrate that low-modulus, low-hardness, creep-compliant, low-strain organic materials that readily deform in response to external pressures and microstructural changes enable stable cell operation at low stack pressures.

Irradiation induces nanoscale holes on the graphene oxide basal plane, causing rapid fragmentation upon hydrogen peroxide treatment. This work provides a route for the pilot-scale production of high-performance nanoscale graphene oxide materials.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Fused in sarcoma (FUS) forms dynamic biomolecular condensates through phase separation, a process associated with stress responses and neurodegenerative diseases. Here, we use in-cell NMR spectroscopy to directly observe condensate formation of the FUS low-complexity (LC) domain in living cells. We identify a two-step process: initial droplet formation followed by time-dependent maturation, characterized by reduced internal mobility. Deletion mutant analysis reveals that while initial condensate formation is driven by collective multivalent interactions, the reversible amyloid core (RAC) region is essential for the subsequent maturation. Intracellular droplets form at concentrations well below the in vitro threshold, which cannot be explained by macromolecular crowding alone. Notably, droplet formation is suppressed under nutrient starvation, suggesting that ATP-dependent cellular activities indirectly promote FUS condensation. These findings demonstrate that the metabolically active intracellular environment modulates FUS condensate behavior, providing mechanistic insights into early events in pathological aggregation and establishing a general framework for studying condensates in cells.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Algal organic matter (AOM) has been considered a typical pollutant in algal bloom waters, conventionally managed through flocculation-flotation processes with high carbon footprints. This study presents a paradigm shift by redefining AOM as a functional crosslinker and developing an AOM-induced self-driven flotation (A-SDF) strategy. The approach utilizes active groups in AOM (-COOH/-OH) coordinated with trace amounts of metal coagulants to construct multilevel gel flocs with Al 2 O 3 /FeO(OH) crystalline phases. Remarkably, these flocs not only capture algal cells but also activate dissolved oxygen (DO), inducing DO enrichment-interfacial gas nucleation behavior (DOE-IGNB) and leading to microbubbles (MBs) formation at the floc interface under mild turbulence. The process achieved efficient removal of algal cells (82–95%), turbidity (86–95%), and AOM (45–79%) within 2 min without external aeration. Compared with existing technologies, the carbon footprint, treatment time, and economic cost were reduced by 66.08–96.90%, 71.67–96.00%, and 50.55–97.67%, respectively, while residual metal concentrations remained well below drinking water standards. Density functional theory calculations confirmed strong DO adsorption by tetrahedral AlO 4 /FeO 4 lattices as the molecular mechanism driving DOE-IGNB. By repurposing AOM as a resource and activating endogenous DO, this work provides a universal carbon-neutral pathway for sustainable algal bloom management worldwide.

candidates.title: A wearable reconfigurable surface electrode network for spatiotemporal control of hand motor output
candidates.authors: Kening Gong, Li Jiang, Siyang Qiu, Xueai Li, Ming Cheng, Xiaoran Tang, Changhao Yan, Lijia Guo, Bangchu Yang, Wenhao Wu, Shilong Wang, Chunhao Peng, Hong Liu
candidates.abstract: Abstract Transcutaneous electrical stimulation can elicit hand movements by activating peripheral nerves and muscles. Here, we present a wearable system integrating programmable constant-current stimulation, a flexible 32-electrode forearm array with full-array active–return routing, and real-time path and parameter updating. Human-derived skin–electrode load tests showed a mean current-delivery accuracy of 94.0%, while four-hour reassessment showed 93.5% within-participant action-category agreement. Using reconfigurable active–return routing and an anatomy-informed two-level traversal strategy, we established current-path-to-action maps spanning 12 wrist and hand action categories, with spatial patterns broadly consistent with superficial forearm flexor and extensor compartments. Data-glove and inertial measurements quantified parameter-dependent finger-joint responses and action-specific wrist rotations. The mapped actions were sequentially combined for feedback-guided, stimulation-assisted task-level hand operation, supporting wearable functional electrical stimulation for task-oriented hand assistance and rehabilitation research.

candidates.title: Giant nonlinear optical responses in the visible via lattice-controlled cascade amplification of photon avalanche
candidates.authors: Ye Yuan, Zizhao Wen, Zining Yuan, Yue Ni, Qiuqiang Zhan
candidates.abstract: The photon avalanche effect exhibits a large optical nonlinear response, which is crucial for advancement in super-resolution imaging and optical sensing. However, photon avalanche systems with nonlinearity exceeding 100 remain confined to a single band in the near-infrared region, where standard detectors have low sensitivity. Here, we show that a cascade amplified photon avalanche strategy via lattice reconstruction to address these limitations. Introducing lutetium substitution into the host lattice enhances interionic energy exchange and cross-relaxation, activating multiple visible emission channels of holmium and erbium ions with amplified nonlinearities. A nonlinearity order of up to 560 is achieved in ~216 nm nanoparticles, while 43 nm nanoparticles retain a nonlinearity of 183 and enable super-resolution microscopy with 28 nm lateral resolution. We further demonstrate multi-color super-resolution microscopy and sub-cellular bioimaging. Benefiting from high detection efficiency and flexible wavelength selection, cascade amplified photon avalanche nanoprobes are promising for ultrasensitive sensing and super-resolution lithography beyond optical imaging. This work extends and amplifies the nonlinear response of Tm³⁺ photon avalanche into the highly detectable visible region with optical nonlinearities exceeding 550, enabling sound 28-nm spatial resolution and multi-channel bioimaging application.

candidates.title: Basal mantle motion causes Pacific hotspot drift
candidates.authors: Xianzhi Cao, Sanzhong Li, Nicolas Flament, Yanhui Suo, Zhaoxia Jiang, Heda Wang, Dingshan Deng, Qiuling Liu
candidates.abstract: Abstract Hotspot-based reference frames are foundational to plate reconstructions yet increasing evidence indicates that individual Pacific hotspots have migrated over time. How the overall motion of Pacific hotspots relates to the evolution of the underlying Pacific basal mantle structure (BMS), the inferred source of Pacific mantle plumes, remains elusive. Here we combine plate reference frame analysis with global mantle flow simulations to quantify the average motion of Pacific hotspots and compare it with the predicted motion of the Pacific BMS. Comparisons between Pacific fixed-hotspot reference frames and other absolute reference frames suggest an average southward migration of Pacific hotspots of ~5–10° from 80 Ma. Mantle flow models driven by plate reconstructions independently predict comparable southward average migration of Pacific plumes and the underlying Pacific BMS. In the models, the coupled BMS-plume migration is driven by greater subduction flux along the northern Pacific than along the southern Pacific between ~80-45 Ma, which generated persistent southward lower-mantle flow. Our results indicate that the average drift of Pacific hotspots is linked to the motion of the Pacific BMS, highlighting dynamic coupling between surface hotspot motion and basal mantle evolution.

candidates.title: Atomic-resolution insights into interactions of rifampicin and rifamycin derivatives with orphan CYP143 of M. tuberculosis
candidates.authors: Andrei Gilep, Christopher MacCarthy, Marianna Karpova, Tatsiana Varaksa, Irina Grabovec, Veronika Karpushenkova, Leonid Kaluzhskiy, Evgeniy Yablokov, Ivan Kapranov, Sergey Bukhdruker, Elizaveta Dronova, Yuqi Yang, Tatsiana Sushko, Alena Karputs, Kouhei Tsumoto, Valentin Borshchevskiy, Natallia Strushkevich
candidates.abstract: Analysis of drug-resistant strains of M. tuberculosis identified a Gly334Ala mutation in the orphan CYP143 gene, located within the ESX-5 secretion cluster. Guided by this clinical association, we tested the frontline antitubercular agent rifampicin as a CYP143 ligand. Atomic-resolution structures reveal a closed binding mode of rifampicin above the heme, which we also observed for other natural and synthetic rifamycins. The high quality of crystallographic data for both the wild type and mutant structures allowed us to track ligand-induced changes from the active site to the meander, the binding site for the redox partner. Consistent with this, the structure of a CYP143–ligand–redox partner complex confirms that these conformational changes are directly coupled to ligand binding. The structure of CYP143 with a selective inhibitor provides a template for rational drug design. Together, these results advance the understanding of rifampicin resistance/tolerance and the role of the orphan CYPome of M. tuberculosis. The study reveals how the mutation associated with drug resistance facilitates the binding of rifampicin to the orphan enzyme of tubercular bacilli, thereby influencing protein-protein interactions. The findings explore pathogen adaptation mechanisms.

candidates.title: Diabetes subtyping without HbA1c enhances identification of severe insulin-deficient diabetes
candidates.authors: Martin Schön, Oana P. Zaharia, Christian Binsch, Huishu Lin, Claudia H. T. Tam, Cadmon K. P. Lim, Gechang Yu, Klaus Strassburger, Tim Mori, Gidon J. Bönhof, Alexander Strom, Katsiaryna Prystupa, Kálmán B. Bódis, Iryna Yurchenko, Dania M. Mendez Cardenas, Yanislava Karusheva, Graciela E. Delgado, Marcus E. Kleber, Sema Kaya, Rainer Guthoff, Sandra Trenkamp, Volker Burkart, Dan Ziegler, Christian Herder, Oliver Kuss, Juliana C. N. Chan, Winfried März, Ronald C. W. Ma, Michael Roden, Robert Wagner, ,
candidates.abstract: Abstract Data-driven subtyping of diabetes can be affected by disease duration and treatment. We propose a modified procedure waiving the use of HbA1c, and only using BMI, age at diagnosis, insulin secretion and insulin sensitivity. Participants of the German Diabetes Study (GDS, N = 940), the Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Health (LURIC) cohort ( N = 794) and the Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank (HKDB) ( N = 7959) were subtyped by including (w/HbA1c) and then by leaving out HbA1c (w/oHbA1c). In GDS, subtyping w/oHbA1c increased the prevalence of severe insulin-deficient diabetes (SIDD) from 3.3% to 22.1%. Cumulative incidence of diabetic retinopathy differed when comparing SIDD and the other clusters using both approaches (w/HbA1c: SIDD 16.1%, P log-rank = 0.027; w/oHbA1c: SIDD 14.4%, p log-rank < 0.001), with higher discriminative ability w/oHbA1c (AUROC: 0.74 vs 0.66 w/HbA1c, p = 0.049). The discrimination of future insulin secretion failure in SIDD was also better w/oHbA1c ( p AUROC = 0.011). In LURIC, subtyping w/oHbA1c also increased the prevalence of SIDD from 3.0% to 11.3% and showed lower all-cause mortality for SIDD compared to insulin resistant ( p = 0.035) and age-related ( p = 0.005) diabetes subtypes. Finally, in HKDB, subtyping w/oHbA1c also increased the prevalence of SIDD from 29.2% to 35.7% without attenuating its association with diabetic retinopathy, supporting preserved subtype discrimination in an independent cohort. The refined algorithm excluding HbA1c improves the detection of the diabetes subtype with severe insulin deficiency and its complications in already treated persons, although further validation in more diverse populations is needed to establish its broader generalizability.

candidates.title: Excited-state twisted intramolecular charge transfer enables reversible light control of rhodamine-graphene binding
candidates.authors: Giovanni M. Beneventi, Yilin He, Xuliang Qian, Matteo Andrea Lucherelli, Martina Hartinger, Konstantin Benthues, Norbert Jux, Alejandro Cadranel, Carolin Müller, Huajian Gao, Alberto Bianco, Dirk Guldi
candidates.abstract: Abstract Reversible light control of supramolecular interactions underpins fundamental processes in nature, inspiring artificial molecular devices and adaptive materials. Existing approaches rely on light-modulated interconversion between ground-state species characterized by distinct binding properties. Here, we introduce twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) as an excited-state specific lever to modulate dye–surface adhesion. Using rhodamine B base (Rhb) as the photoactive species, we combine femtosecond spectroscopy with theoretical calculations to provide a direct observation of TICT formation and its thermal equilibrium with the locally excited state. We show that the associated dihedral twisting and charge redistribution weaken Rhb-graphene binding, enabling light-induced dye desorption in water. Molecular dynamics simulations corroborate that the out-of-plane TICT conformations induce steric hindrance against the graphene basal plane, significantly reducing the binding affinity and lowering the thermodynamic barrier of the dye-surface desorption. This synergy between experiment and theory establishes excited-state conformational dynamics as a general strategy to control supramolecular interactions in host-guest systems in physiological conditions, with implications for sensing, delivery, and materials science.

candidates.title: Preventing data leakage in neural decoding
candidates.authors: Robert Wong, Michael H. McCullough, Tianfeng Lu, Shuyu I. Zhu, Geoffrey J. Goodhill
candidates.abstract: Abstract Neural decoding is a widely-used machine learning technique for investigating how behavior, perception and cognition are represented in neural activity. However without careful application data leakage can occur, where information from the test set contaminates the training set, leading to biased estimates of decoding performance and potentially invalidating biological conclusions. Here we show that leakage can be introduced in neural decoding studies by common supervised and unsupervised preprocessing steps, including dimensionality reduction. We reveal that in some cases leakage can paradoxically decrease decoding performance relative to unbiased estimates, and we provide theoretical analyses explaining how this occurs. We also show that, for autocorrelated neural time series, randomized k-fold cross-validation can dramatically overstate decoding performance. Based on these findings, we provide detailed recommendations for avoiding data leakage in neural decoding.

candidates.title: Iron supplementation in iron-deficient Kenyan infants: a randomised controlled trial of vaccine immunogenicity
candidates.authors: Nicole U. Stoffel, Suzane Nyilima, Edith Mwasi, Gerco den Hartog, Florens Lohrmann, Petter Brodin, Hal Drakesmith, Simon Karanja, Michael B. Zimmermann
candidates.abstract: Iron deficiency is common in early infancy, but whether supplementation improves vaccine immunogenicity is uncertain. In this randomised, double-blind trial in coastal Kenya (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04744818), 288 breastfed, iron-deficient infants aged six weeks received daily oral iron (3 mg/kg/day; n = 143) or control (n = 145) until 24 weeks during routine immunisation; follow-up continued to 52 weeks. Primary outcomes were diphtheria and pertussis IgG responses during supplementation. Secondary outcomes were antibody responses to oral and inactivated poliovirus, Haemophilus influenzae type b, tetanus, hepatitis B, and 10-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine. Vaccines were given at 6, 10 and 14 weeks. Iron supplementation reduced iron deficiency (OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.34–0.71; p < 0.001) and iron deficiency anaemia (0.63, 0.42–0.96; p = 0.031). Adjusted geometric mean ratios (iron/control) for antibody concentrations were 0.82 (0.67–1.00) for diphtheria, 0.83 (0.64–1.07) for pertussis toxin, 0.82 (0.66–1.02) for filamentous haemagglutinin and 0.80 (0.59–1.10) for pertactin. Antibody responses to most other vaccines did not significantly differ. Seroprotection and adverse-event frequencies did not differ significantly between groups. Iron supplementation from 6 to 24 weeks safely reduced iron deficiency anaemia but was associated with modestly lower diphtheria and pertussis vaccine responses, while responses to other routine childhood vaccines were mostly unaffected. In a trial of 288 Kenyan infants, daily iron supplements reduced iron-deficiency anaemia but did not improve antibody responses to routine vaccines. Diphtheria antibody levels were modestly lower with iron, while seroprotection rates were similar.

candidates.title: An interaction module for mitochondrial ATP synthase assembly and maintenance in seed plants
candidates.authors: Mengmeng Yang, Yuqi Hou, Wumei Qu, Mingchao An, Tiantian Li, Lu Liang, Kailun Li, Jiaqi Yan, Xiaoyi Huang, Jiahui Gao, Xian-Ao Wang, Jianfei Ma, Hongchun Yang, Lei Li
candidates.abstract: ATP synthase and its dimerization are essential for cristae formation and mitochondrial biogenesis. In plants, the absence of canonical j and k subunits raises the question of how ATP synthase assembly and dimerization are supported in this lineage. We identify MTF5, a fast-turnover, seed plant-specific protein critical for embryogenesis and mitochondrial biogenesis. Loss of MTF5 causes embryo arrest and altered mitochondrial morphology. A conditional complementation line partially rescues the embryo-lethal phenotype but shows growth defects and mitochondrial morphology changes. MTF5 interacts with another fast-turnover protein, MTF5P, and co-migrates with ATP synthase dimerization-associated subunits, supporting a role in ATP synthase assembly and maintenance. Structural predictions reveal a helical architecture comprising a long central α-helix flanked by shorter helices, but do not establish direct correspondence with canonical j and k subunits. Our findings uncover an interaction module for ATP synthase assembly and maintenance that is essential for seed plant growth and development. Mitochondrial ATP synthase is crucial for cellular energy production, but how it is assembled and maintained in plants is not fully uncovered. Here, the authors show that MTF5 and MTF5P form an interaction module essential for ATP synthase assembly and maintenance in seed plants.

candidates.title: Directional codes for quantum LDPC error correction on square and hexagonal grid architectures
candidates.authors: György P. Gehér, David Byfield, Archibald Ruban
candidates.abstract: Utility-scale quantum computing requires quantum error correction to protect quantum information against noise. Superconducting hardware is a promising platform for fault-tolerant computation, but its typically two-dimensional nearest-neighbour connectivity restricts the variety of quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes that can be implemented efficiently. Here we introduce directional codes, a family of qLDPC codes compatible with square-grid and, in some cases, hexagonal-grid architectures. The key idea is to use the iSWAP gate to measure long range stabilisers using only local interactions, without requiring additional connectivity. We evaluate directional codes using a superconducting-inspired circuit-level Pauli noise model and compare them to the rotated toric code and bivariate bicycle codes. The best directional code family considered matches the logical error rate of the rotated toric code at physical error rate p = 10−3 but requires only a quarter to a third of the number of physical qubits to encode a given number of logical qubits. Superconducting qubit platforms usually support only nearest-neighbour connectivity, complicating the implementation of efficient quantum low-density parity check codes. Here, the authors propose a family of qLDPC codes that replace long-range connections with local iSWAP-based circuits for stabiliser measurements, while outperforming the rotated toric code.

candidates.title: A small RNA regulates iron homeostasis and host mucus colonization in Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron
candidates.authors: Thomas Guest, Ryan T. Fansler, Gianluca Prezza, Gohar Mädler, Hannah Schlauch, Wenhan Zhu, Alexander J. Westermann
candidates.abstract: Abstract Symbiotic bacteria in the human intestinal microbiota provide many pivotal functions to human health and occupy distinct biogeographic niches within the gut. Yet the molecular basis underlying niche-specific colonization remains poorly defined. To address this, we conducted a time-resolved dual RNA-seq experiment to simultaneously monitor the transcriptional co-adaptations of human commensal Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron and human gut epithelial cells in a hypoxic, mucus-producing, epithelial co-culture system. Comparative transcriptomic analysis of mucus-associated versus supernatant Bacteroides populations unveiled small RNAs (sRNAs) that are differentially regulated between spatially segregated subpopulations. Among these, we identified IroR as a key sRNA that facilitates B . thetaiotaomicron adaptation to iron limitation and host glycan availability, partly by modulating expression of capsule-associated surface states. This work provides new insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of gut colonization and underscores a previously underappreciated role for bacterial sRNAs in shaping mutualistic interactions between the human microbiota and the gut epithelium.

candidates.title: Tomato NLR R1L mediates SlSPL3 degradation to trigger a growth-to-defense switch against Phytophthora infestans
candidates.authors: Ziyu Wang, Xiaofeng Tang, Feng Zhang, Yu Xu, Xue Fang, Ruoxi Lu, Hongtao Wang, Wangmei Ren, Man Huang, Zhiping Liu, Yongsheng Liu, Min Miao
candidates.abstract: Intracellular nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) receptors activate effector-triggered immunity (ETI), a key branch of plant immunity conferring robust resistance. The downstream signaling mechanisms of ETI receptors remain unclear. We characterize tomato NLR protein R1L that specifically recognizes the Phytophthora infestans effector AVR1. R1L is predominantly cytoplasmic and partially relocalizes into the nucleus upon infection. With helper SlNRC1, R1L and AVR1 trigger a hypersensitive response (HR). R1L positively regulates tomato immunity against P. infestans. Yeast two-hybrid screening identified SlSPL3, a positive regulator of growth and development, as a direct R1L interactor. SlSPL3 binds the GTAC-box motif in the SlLTP3 promoter and activates this negative immune regulator. R1L counteracts SlSPL3-mediated immune suppression by promoting the ubiquitin-mediated degradation of SlSPL3. Thus, the AVR1-R1L-SlSPL3-SlLTP3 module mediates a growth-immunity trade-off. In uninfected plants, SlSPL3 promotes growth and suppresses immunity via SlLTP3. Upon infection, R1L-mediated SlSPL3 degradation activates immunity and represses growth. This study elucidates a pathogen perception-transcriptional reprogramming-immunity axis, offering insights into plant defense and growth-immunity balance. candidates.authors: Janna Wilhelmsen, Longzhu Liu, Harry Miyosi Silalahi, Suraya Kazi, Giancarlo Cincotti, Shangzhi Chen, Dongqing Lin, Yulong Duan, Magnus P. Jonsson
candidates.abstract: Abstract Phase-gradient metasurfaces shape optical wavefronts through arrays of optical nanoantennas acting as metaatoms. While dynamic tunability forms a major frontier in this area, direct electrical switching of metaatoms operating in the visible has remained challenging. Here, we present an exciton-based metaatom that is electrically tunable and operates in the visible. Its function originates from an excitonic absorption band of a dedoped conjugated polymer, which together with low background permittivity induces optical metallicity in the visible. This allows anisotropic nanostructures to exhibit polarization-dependent optical response through localized surface exciton-polariton resonances, rather than plasmons or dielectric Mie resonances. This function can be fully switched off through reversible doping by small bias potentials, which turns off the exciton-induced metallicity. Our study details the mechanism of these metaatoms and demonstrates their use in electrically tunable phase-gradient metasurfaces for visible light, including erasable and rewritable holograms. This work thereby establishes a class of electrically switchable exciton-based metaatoms and expands the design space of dynamic visible metaoptics.

candidates.abstract: The exponential surge in artificial intelligence computing power demand is driving a transition from electrons to photons across the infrastructure. Although integrated photonics has revolutionized communications and computing, its scaling for large-scale information processing is constrained by monolithic scalability, modulation efficiency, and multi-chip integration. Through function disaggregation, HyPec partitions high-performance active modulation from the 3D photonic routing network. This chiplet architecture facilitates seamless multi-chip connectivity across diverse material platforms to achieve aggregate performance beyond monolithic limits, thereby allowing the system to scale through the addition of functional chiplets. To validate the advantages of this architecture, we experimentally built a co-packaged photonic computing chiplet system that implements a scalable graph solver and further identifies critical protein residues in structural biology networks. This work establishes a scalable hardware path for integrated photonic computing, with broader implications for high-density optical interconnects and photonic quantum information systems. Here we show, using three-dimensional tissue imaging, in vivo calcium recordings, single-cell transcriptomics, and chemogenetics in mice, that the mesenteric lymph node (mLN) harbours functionally antagonistic neural circuits that govern T cell fate. These findings establish the mLN as an autonomic rheostat for intestinal immunity. candidates.abstract: Abstract Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with hepatic and extrahepatic morbidity, but non-invasive tests provide indirect, largely cross-sectional risk estimates, limiting continuous and individualised prognostication. Here we develop AEGIS-MASLD, an explainable deep learning framework integrating dual-stain liver biopsy images, clinical data and longitudinal lifestyle records to predict 13 MASLD-related multisystem outcomes. This retrospective multicentre study included 814 adults with biopsy-confirmed MASLD without baseline comorbidities, followed for a median of 203 months. The model was developed in 546 patients from three Chinese centres using five-fold cross-validation and externally validated in 268 patients from six independent centres. In external validation, the model predicted 12 non-fatal outcomes with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.766–0.867, outperforming conventional histological and non-invasive fibrosis scores. All-cause mortality was evaluated separately using pathology and laboratory data. Annual risk estimates for non-fatal outcomes were updated as lifestyle exposures changed. Tissue analyses identified 24 histopathological phenotype clusters, linking fibrotic clusters to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, and inflammatory clusters to cardiovascular events. These findings suggest that digital pathology analysis of routinely obtained biopsy material, combined with clinical and lifestyle data, could support individualised multisystem risk assessment and follow-up in patients with MASLD undergoing biopsy-based evaluation.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Continuous-wave-pumped optical parametric oscillators (OPOs) provide an exciting avenue to generate coherent radiation at wavelength regions that are difficult to reach by traditional semiconductor optical amplifiers. However, attaining ultra-narrow linewidth operation in OPOs requires pump lasers with exceptional purity to begin with. Here, we demonstrate an integrated Kerr nonlinear OPO featuring an integrated external cavity based on ultralow-loss silicon nitride that results in a continuous-wave signal with a 15-fold intrinsic linewidth reduction compared to the pump, down to 10 Hz. Our numerical analysis indicates that the intrinsic linewidth can be reduced below the Schawlow-Townes limit of a single-cavity OPO depending on the feedback length and strength of the external cavity. Utilizing an integrated erbium-doped waveguide amplifier, we further demonstrate sub-Hz intrinsic linewidth coherent oscillation. These results establish an effective pathway towards chip-scale ultra-coherent light sources with high power and broad wavelength tunability, opening new opportunities for high-precision optical sensing and detection.

candidates.abstract: Forests are natural coolers of Earth’s land surface temperatures. However, the local biophysical cooling provided by forest is often constrained by trade-off between expanding forest areas and competing land uses, which has challenged both policymakers and scientists for decades. Restoring forest canopy structural complexity has long been viewed as a promising nature-based strategy to alleviate this constrain, yet its effectiveness and underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood at the global scale. Using satellite-derived land surface temperature and LiDAR-based measurements of canopy structures, we show that increasing canopy structural complexity enhances local land surface cooling across most global forests (90.0%). The cooling potential of vertical canopy complexity consistently exceeds that of horizontal crown cover density, which has been long overlooked. By aligning canopy structure complexity of managed forests with that of nearby intact forests, we estimate a potential reduction of 0.25 ± 0.001 °C in local land surface temperature globally. Our findings provide insights into strengthening the climate regulation of existing forests through the ecological restoration of forest canopy structure complexity and suggest a space-efficient management strategy that complements, rather than substitutes for, forest conservation and afforestation. Forest biophysical cooling is constrained by limited land for afforestation. This study suggest that increasing canopy structural complexity enhances forest biophysical cooling by 0.25 °C globally, offering a land-efficient forest management strategy.

candidates.title: Directional atomic-ordering gradients enable fatigue-resistant superelasticity in carbon tube aerogels
candidates.authors: De Lu, Ziyan Li, Chuankui Xiao, Min Niu, Kang Peng, Shuhai Jia, Wenhao Tong, Mengjie Li, Pengcheng Zhang, Lei Su, Yilun Liu, Huasong Qin, Hongjie Wang
candidates.abstract: Abstract Elastic inorganic aerogels are highly attractive for weight-sensitive applications in extreme environments, yet integrating high strength, large-strain recoverability and fatigue resistance within a single architecture remains a longstanding challenge. Here we show that directional atomic-ordering gradients in carbon tube aerogels provide a structural route to overcoming this trade-off. Guided by finite-element analysis, we create atomic-ordering gradient junctions through stepwise-modulated chemical vapor deposition, producing a radial increase in carbon ordering across load-bearing tube walls and inter-tube junctions. Multiscale characterization and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the directional gradient enables the outer crystalline region to function as a sliding-enabled stress-relief layer, thereby promoting stress delocalization, suppressing bond rupture and reducing irreversible energy dissipation before network densification becomes dominant. As a result, the directional-gradient aerogel sustains reversible compression up to 95% strain, reaches a maximum stress of 8.0 MPa, and retains ~87% of its initial maximum stress after 10,000 cycles at 90% strain with only ~6% permanent deformation. These findings show that controlling atomic ordering at carbon tube junctions offers an effective way to improve the mechanical robustness and fatigue resistance of highly compressible porous solids.

candidates.title: Kinetic Pathway for Electron Energization during Strong Guide-Field Magnetic Reconnection
candidates.authors: Sonu Yadav, Thomas Rood, Earl Scime, Peiyun Shi, Jongsoo Yoo, Gregory G. Howes
candidates.abstract: Here, we present direct, time-resolved measurements of resonant wave–particle interactions during strong guide-field magnetic reconnection in the PHAse Space MApping (PHASMA) experiment. Correlated measurements of lower-hybrid drift waves (LHDWs) and electron velocity distribution functions (EVDFs), obtained from reproducible reconnection discharges, reveal that coherent finite- k ∥ LHDWs develop at the reconnection separatrix and produce discrete velocity-space enhancements within the thermal electron population at velocities matching the measured parallel phase velocities, v_{ph}=omega/k_{}. As the wave activity saturates and decays, these resonant structures broaden into plateaus on a timescale of ~2 microsecond, in quantitative agreement with the quasilinear relaxation time independently inferred from the measured wave amplitudes, coherence times, and plateau widths. These measurements establish a direct experimental link between lower-hybrid wave activity and resonant electron energization during magnetic reconnection, identifying a kinetic pathway for magnetic-energy conversion.

candidates.title: Efficient Integrated Quantum Memory Based on a Waveguide Cavity
candidates.authors: Pei-Xi Liu, Yi-Xin Xiao, Tian-Xiang Zhu, Zhe-Kai You, Zong-Quan Zhou, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo
candidates.abstract: Efficient integrated quantum memories are a key enabling technology for scalable quantum networks and photonic quantum processors, yet their efficiencies have remained below the critical threshold of 90% required for demanding applications. Here we demonstrate an integrated photonic quantum memory with a storage-and-retrieval efficiency of 90.2(4)% for single-photon-level weak coherent pulses and a storage fidelity of 99.3(1)% for time-bin qubits, using a waveguide cavity fabricated in Pr 3 + : Y 2 S i O 5 . This performance is enabled by the high absorption-to-loss ratio of Pr 3 + ions in a low-loss waveguide cavity, combined with a time-reversal technique to overcome the dispersion-limited cavity linewidth and a novel spectral preparation scheme that creates a clean transparency window while utilizing a single class of ions that is compatible for spin-wave storage. Our results establish the first integrated photonic memory beyond the 90% efficiency threshold, representing an important step toward applications that demand the highest performance, such as scalable quantum repeaters, photonic quantum computing and device-independent quantum key distribution.

candidates.title: Enhanced Coherence in the Periodically Driven Two-Dimensional XY Model
candidates.authors: Duilio De Santis, Marios H. Michael, Sambuddha Chattopadhyay, Andrea Cavalleri, Gil Refael, Patrick A. Lee, Eugene A. Demler
candidates.abstract: Strong optical drives have been shown to induce transient superconducting-like response in materials above their equilibrium T c . Many of these materials already exhibit short-range superconducting correlations in equilibrium. This motivates the question: can external driving enhance coherence in systems with superconducting correlations but no long-range order? We explore this scenario in the two-dimensional XY model with a periodically modulated stiffness using overdamped Langevin dynamics. We find that, even though the modulation leaves the average coupling unchanged, the drive can markedly increase long-range, time-averaged correlations in systems well above the equilibrium Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless temperature. The outcome depends on the ratio of the drive frequency to the intrinsic relaxation rate: faster drives primarily heat the system, suppressing correlations and conductivity. For slower drives, the optical conductivity is modified so that the real part exhibits a prolonged effective Drude scattering time, while the imaginary part has a strengthened low-frequency 1 / ω behavior. We map out these regimes across temperature, frequency, and amplitude, and rationalize them via simple analytics and vortex-thermalization arguments. Overall, we identify a generic nonequilibrium route to enhance coherence in XY-like systems, with potential relevance to experiments reporting light-induced superconducting-like response.

candidates.title: Quantum Correlations and Dissipative Blockade of Polaritons in a Tunable Fiber Cavity
candidates.authors: Gian-Marco Schnüriger, Martin Kroner, Emre Togan, Patrick Knüppel, Aymeric Delteil, Stefan Fält, Werner Wegscheider, Ataç Imamoğlu
candidates.abstract: Cavity exciton–polaritons are quasiparticles that form when quantum well excitons hybridize with a cavity mode. Here, we carry out photon correlation measurements under continuous wave resonant laser excitation to demonstrate quantum correlations between cavity–polaritons. Our experiments reveal an unexpectedly strong dependence of polariton interactions on cavity–exciton detuning. When the polaritons are predominantly exciton-like, we observe a transition from photon antibunching to bunching as the laser is tuned across the polariton resonance, in agreement with a simple Kerr-nonlinearity model. When the lower-branch polariton energy is tuned to induce a two-polariton Feshbach resonance with the biexciton mode, the degree of polariton antibunching becomes independent of the laser detuning: we explain our finding by invoking a dissipative blockade mechanism arising from large biexciton broadening. Our experiments demonstrate that the strong polariton blockade regime would be achieved by reducing the polariton decay rate by a factor of 10.

candidates.abstract: We present the conservative dynamics of compact binaries to third order in the post-Minkowskian approximation in a theory that extends general relativity by a massless scalar field coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet invariant. We employ the effective field theory approach to construct the effective action of binary systems by integrating out the metric and scalar degrees of freedom that mediate the gravitational interactions between the two bodies. We derive analytical expressions for the scattering impulse and the deflection angle to third order in the post-Minkowskian expansion. Our results are found to be in agreement, in the overlapping regimes, with state-of-the-art calculations in the post-Newtonian/post-Minkowskian theory.

candidates.title: Spin Excitons Modulated by Magnetic Orders in a Magnetic Weyl Semimetal NdAlSi
candidates.authors: Bo Zhang, Junbo Liao, Lihao Xia, Zhentao Huang, Yanyan Shangguan, Shufan Cheng, Hao Xu, Zihang Song, Shuai Dong, Maofeng Wu, Wei Wang, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Mitsutaka Nakamura, Song Bao, Zhao-Yang Dong, Shun-Li Yu, Jian-Xin Li, Jinsheng Wen
candidates.abstract: We report the observation of dispersive spin excitons in the rare-earth magnetic Weyl semimetal NdAlSi through comprehensive thermodynamic and inelastic neutron scattering measurements. Notably, the behavior of spin excitons is strongly modulated by magnetic order: they remain dispersive in the paramagnetic phase, shift to higher energies and broaden in the incommensurate antiferromagnetic phase, and split into distinct branches in the commensurate ferrimagnetic phase. To elucidate the microscopic origin of this evolution, we construct an effective crystal electric field (CEF)–exchange model and calculate the excitation spectra within the random-phase approximation. This framework consistently accounts for the observed excitation dispersions and mode splitting by incorporating two magnetic-order-dependent effects: an effective renormalization of the local CEF environment associated with the concomitant reconstruction of the itinerant electronic structure across the magnetic phases, and exchange-generated molecular fields that lift the Kramers degeneracy. Our findings reveal the interplay among localized 4f states, itinerant electrons, and magnetic order, and establish NdAlSi as a model platform for studying collective CEF excitations in rare-earth quantum materials.

candidates.authors: Gyungchoon Go, Se Kwon Kim
candidates.abstract: We identify a previously unrecognized spin-lattice coupling allowed by broken inversion symmetry that can be viewed as a lattice analogue of electronic Rashba spin-orbit coupling. In the low-frequency regime, where magnons are integrated out, its interplay with the conventional magnetoelastic coupling generates a kineo-elastic term that couples strain and lattice velocity, giving rise to nonreciprocal phonon velocity. We further analyze the full magnon-phonon spectrum and find that the competition between interfacial spin-lattice and magnetoelastic couplings leads to directional hybridization and absorption, yielding asymmetric phonon propagation lengths for opposite directions. Our results indicate that such interfacial spin-lattice coupling can provide an efficient route to nonreciprocal phonon propagation in magnetic heterostructures with strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling.

candidates.abstract: In molecular simulations, machine learning force fields can achieve accuracy at a lower cost but remain limited in the explicit modeling of electrons. In this Letter, we develop an electron-aware machine learning force field in which an excess electron of interest is modeled quantum mechanically, while the remaining short-range interactions and long-range Coulombic forces are machine learned to reproduce a density functional theory calculation. We demonstrate the method on the solvated electron in bulk water and its reaction with a hydronium ion. From an enhanced sampling simulation, we determine the equilibrium constant, and thus the reaction free energy, which is also consistent with experimental measurements.

candidates.title: Microscopic Theory of Spin Polarons in Chern Ferromagnets
candidates.authors: Qiang Gao, Eslam Khalaf
candidates.abstract: We develop a microscopic theory of charged excitations in an SU(2) Chern ferromagnet and obtain closed-form wavefunctions for a hierarchy of charge-$e$ spin polaron states binding an arbitrary number of spin flips. In an ideal Chern-$1$ band with a normal-ordered contact interaction, we show that these polarons are exact eigenstates of the Hamiltonian with the same energy as single-hole excitations. Away from this ideal limit, we promote these states to a variational family by introducing a single size parameter and a geometry-informed single-particle dressing. Our momentum-space wavefunctions admit two equivalent representations: a ratio of Jastrow factors of Weierstrass functions of relative momenta or an antisymmetrized geminal product of particle-hole wavefunctions. The latter enables efficient evaluation of overlaps and expectation values for large system sizes and many spin flips. Benchmarking in the lowest Landau level, the single-spin-flip ansatz achieves $\gtrsim 99\%$ overlap with exact diagonalization and accurately captures binding energies, while the multi-spin-flip energies interpolate smoothly toward the large-texture (skyrmion) regime. For Chern bands with tunable quantum geometry, we find that interaction-generated single particle dispersion quickly destabilizes the spin polarons once quantum geometry becomes sufficiently non-uniform. When such dispersion is suppressed, however, the bound states persist deeper into the non-uniform regime, with the binding energy slowly decreasing and the bound state becoming larger as the quantum geometry becomes more concentrated. Our results provide a microscopic foundation for analyzing doped Chern ferromagnets in moiré platforms and lay the groundwork for variational wavefunctions of multi-polaron excitations and phases.
